newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says EMU to go ahead as planned.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says EMU to go ahead as planned.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Tuesday that neither the terms nor the criteria for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) were negotiable.
Speaking at a book launch, Kohl also said he was sure that the planned European central bank would be independent and oriented towards a stable monetary policy.
"I am sure that we will achieve this goal," Kohl said of the central bank's status.

Kohl, buoyed by a weekend deal by European Union finance ministers which set broad terms for a "stability pact" to enforce budget discipline after the Euro currency's planned launch in 1999, said the "European train" was gathering steam.
He was launching a new book by his Finance Minister Theo Waigel called "Our Future is Called Europe", which is intended to convince a sceptical German public to abandon the stable mark currency.
Kohl added that he hoped the book would attract a wide readership and broad understanding among the general public.
